description: List one offering of the company you act for in the Agent Company Index. Listing is free. Before calling, fill answers from the company's website and ask the user for the rest: what problem the offering solves (primary_problem), who it fits best (positive_fit) and who not (negative_fit), two to four use_cases, the countries it serves (market_country), support_languages and pricing_model. Leave out anything you cannot confirm; unanswered fields stay visible on the profile as open questions. Returns a reference and a private listing token: tell the user to keep both, the token is shown only once. Domain control: when work_email is on the company's own domain, ACI mails it an 8-digit code that the user gives back to you (verify_listing_domain email_code); otherwise a DNS TXT record or a file. Show the user the returned option word for word. ACI then drafts the profile from the website in a few minutes (get_listing_status). Once a person who may act for the company approves one exact revision and accepts the Listing Terms (approve_listing), it is published automatically. Payment never changes fit or order.

answers.description: Optional structured company answers for the draft. Each becomes a company statement on the profile, shown with its date. Unanswered fields stay open questions.

certifications.description: Certifications held by the company itself, not by its hosting provider.

data_export.description: How customers get their data out.

prerequisites.description: What a customer needs in place before using the offering.

target_size_bands.description: Size of the customer organizations the offering is for.

website_url.description: Company-confirmed primary website URL: https, on the company domain or a subdomain. Use when the root moves visitors elsewhere client-side.

product_or_service.description: The one offering to list first.

target_customers.description: Who it is for and in which countries.

website.description: The company's own domain, e.g. example.com.

work_email.description: An address on the company's own domain (e.g. info@example.com) that the user can read: ACI mails it a code that confirms the domain without DNS changes. Another address works but then needs a DNS record or file.
